classification.difficultyReason: Calculate each increased or remaining amount, then express the restoring difference as a percentage of that changed amount. Selecting the new percentage base links two taught procedures; the four contexts require no additional unsignposted insight.

children.label: a
children.prompt: A shirt originally priced at $\$45$ was increased in price by $100\%$. What percentage discount will restore it to its original price?

children.label: b
children.prompt: The daily passenger total of the Route 58 bus was $460$, and in one year, it increased by $24\%$. What percentage decrease next year would restore it to its original passenger total? Give your answer correct to $2$ decimal places.

answer.short:
$19.36\%$

Express the reduction as a percentage of the increased passenger total.
answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Increased daily total} &= 460\times1.24\\\text{Increased daily total} &= 570.4\\\text{Decrease required} &= \frac{570.4-460}{570.4}\times100\%\\\text{Decrease required} &= \frac{600}{31}\%\\\text{Decrease required} &\approx 19.36\%\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Shafqat had savings of $\$6000$, but he spent $35\%$ of this last year. By what percentage of the new amount must he increase his savings to restore them to their original value? Give your answer correct to $2$ decimal places.

answer.short:
$53.85\%$

Express the amount spent as a percentage of the remaining savings.

children.label: d
children.prompt: The profit of the Arborville Gelatine Factory was $\$86400$, but it then decreased by $42\%$. By what percentage must the profit increase to restore it to its original value? Give your answer correct to $2$ decimal places.

answer.short:
$72.41\%$

Express the lost profit as a percentage of the reduced profit.
